title: Keep Azure Speech authorization inside the application server
classification: Customer architecture policy, not an Azure vulnerability
requirement: The application must not deliver Azure Speech keys, service authorization tokens, Entra tokens, tenant/subscription identifiers or Speech ARM identifiers to browser code, HTTP responses, request URLs, browser logs or recordings. Preserve real-time browser-to-Azure avatar media.
allowedBrowserData: SDP offer/answer including transient ICE username/password and DTLS fingerprint
Ephemeral WebRTC TURN relay configuration, only for an authenticated operator
Opaque application session identifiers and an HttpOnly application authorization cookie
Public Azure service/relay hostnames and media endpoint IPs
nonGoals: Claiming that resource identifiers are authentication secrets
Automatically approving or releasing a production change

acceptance.criterion: No Azure service credential or actual ARM/tenant/subscription identifier in live application responses, URLs or browser console.
Obsolete Speech-token issuing routes return 404 for all tested methods, including when authenticated.

A real browser receives increasing decoded video frames, nonzero video dimensions and inbound audio bytes. Record the actual engine, version and operating system; never claim an untested browser passed.
Unauthenticated or cross-origin billable requests are denied before any provider call.
A synthetic unmodified baseline and base64-obfuscation wrong fix both fail the same boundary policy.
One concurrent session, a 90-second server deadline, bounded start rate and reliable closure.
Evidence labels fixture versus live execution and leaves approval pending human review.
